content:
On Monday, we reported an issue where iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max users were experiencing their devices freezing and then automatically restarting after a failed Face ID authentication. As far as we could tell, the situation appeared to be a software bug rather than a hardware problem.

Apple has confirmed to 9to5Mac that a software update to address this issue is in the works and is expected to roll out early next week.

Although this bug is not affecting all users, based on feedback from social media and 9to5Mac readers, the issue appears to be quite widespread.

We were able to reproduce the issue on an iPhone 18 Pro by covering the face with a hand while attempting to use Face ID to log into the Passwords app. The device immediately became completely unresponsive to touch and force-restarted after a few seconds. Users can subsequently find a panic log in the iPhone analytics data within the Settings app.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max feature a redesigned Face ID sensor system, with the infrared camera relocated beneath the display near the status bar clock, resulting in a 25% reduction in the size of the visible Dynamic Island.

As we reported earlier this week, some customers, believing the issue to be a hardware fault, had already visited Apple Stores to get their devices replaced in an attempt to resolve the restarting problem. To reiterate, it has now been confirmed that a software update will be released, so there is no need to do this.

On a related note, Apple has also just released watchOS 27.0.1 to fix the issue of random restarts affecting Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4.
